history.q: In which year did Nigeria gain independence from Britain?
history.fact: Independence came on 1 October 1960, a date still celebrated every year as Independence Day.

history.q: Which colonial power merged the Northern and Southern Protectorates to form Nigeria in 1914?
history.fact: Frederick Lugard oversaw the merger and became the first Governor-General of the unified colony.

history.q: Nigeria takes its name from which river?
history.fact: Journalist Flora Shaw proposed the name in The Times in 1897 for the British-ruled lands along the river.

history.q: Which coastal city was Nigeria's capital at independence?
history.fact: Lagos remained the capital until December 1991, when the seat of government formally moved to the planned city of Abuja.

history.q: The historic Kingdom of Benin, ruled by a line of Obas, was centred in which present-day Nigerian city?
history.fact: Despite the shared name, it is unrelated to the modern Republic of Benin; its earthen walls were among the largest earthworks ever built.

history.q: The powerful Oyo Empire was built by which people?
history.fact: Ruled by a monarch titled the Alaafin, Oyo used its cavalry to dominate trade routes to the coast in the 17th and 18th centuries.

history.q: Which ancient culture of central Nigeria is famed for its terracotta sculptures and early iron-working?
history.fact: It is named after the village in Kaduna State where tin miners first came across its striking clay figures.

history.q: Which Scottish explorer drowned in the Niger River near Bussa in 1806?
history.fact: Park had already become famous for his first Niger journey, described in his 1799 book 'Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa'.

history.q: In 1963 Nigeria replaced the British monarch as head of state by becoming what?
history.fact: The change took effect on 1 October 1963, exactly three years after independence.

history.q: Which scholar and reformer founded the Sokoto Caliphate in the early 19th century?
history.fact: His son Muhammad Bello founded the city of Sokoto in 1809, and the Sultan of Sokoto remains an influential traditional ruler.

history.q: Which long-lived empire was centred around Lake Chad, including part of today's north-eastern Nigeria?
history.fact: Its later capital, Birnin Gazargamu, lay in what is now Yobe State, and its caravans traded across the Sahara.

history.q: Queen Amina, a celebrated 16th-century ruler in Hausa tradition, led which city-state?
history.fact: Tradition credits her with building earthen walls around towns, still known as 'ganuwar Amina'.

history.q: Which activist led the Abeokuta Women's Union in protests against unfair taxes in the 1940s?
history.fact: Often said to be the first woman in Nigeria to drive a car, she was also the mother of Afrobeat pioneer Fela Kuti.

history.q: Which city is traditionally regarded as the cradle of the Yoruba people?
history.fact: Its ruler, the Ooni of Ife, is among the most revered Yoruba monarchs, and the city's ancient metal heads are world-famous.

history.q: Which engineer and journalist, often called the father of Nigerian nationalism, founded the country's first political party in 1923?
history.fact: His Nigerian National Democratic Party contested Lagos seats created by the 1922 constitution, the first to include elected Africans.

history.q: Which member of the British royal family represented Queen Elizabeth II at Nigeria's independence celebrations in 1960?
history.fact: She formally opened the new nation's first parliament in Lagos during the celebrations.

history.q: The trading city-state of Old Calabar was built by which people?
history.fact: Efik merchants kept written records in English, such as the 18th-century diary of trader Antera Duke.

history.q: How many regions was Nigeria divided into at independence in 1960?
history.fact: The Northern, Western and Eastern Regions each had its own government and premier.

history.q: Which chartered firm, led by George Goldie, governed much of the Niger basin until 1900?
history.fact: When its charter was revoked, its lands passed to the British Crown and formed the core of the Northern Nigeria Protectorate.

history.q: The Aro Confederacy, a powerful Igbo trading network, was centred on which town?
history.fact: Aro traders built networks across the south-east, guided by the renowned Ibini Ukpabi oracle.

history.q: Which ancient Igbo kingdom was led by a priest-king known as the Eze Nri?
history.fact: Nri's influence spread through ritual authority rather than armies, and its culture is linked to the Igbo-Ukwu bronzes.

history.q: The Kwararafa confederacy of the Benue valley is associated with which people?
history.fact: The Jukun king, the Aku Uka, still holds court at Wukari in today's Taraba State.

history.q: Which politician moved the 1953 motion calling for Nigerian self-government by 1956?
history.fact: Self-government did not come in 1956, but the motion helped speed the timetable towards independence in 1960.

history.q: Which pair of explorers traced the lower Niger to its mouth in 1830?
history.fact: Their journey proved that the river empties into the Gulf of Guinea through the many channels of the Niger Delta.

history.q: In which year did Britain annex Lagos as a colony?
history.fact: Lagos became a British colony decades before the rest of present-day Nigeria came under direct British rule.

technology.q: Which commodity has supplied the bulk of Nigeria's export earnings since the 1970s?
technology.fact: Nigeria joined OPEC in 1971, and oil and gas have since provided the large majority of its export revenue.

technology.q: In 1956, oil was first found in commercial quantities in which part of Nigeria?
technology.fact: The discovery well was at Oloibiri, in today's Bayelsa State, and exports began in 1958.

technology.q: Nigeria is the world's largest producer of which starchy root crop?
technology.fact: Cassava is processed into everyday staples such as garri and fufu.

technology.q: Which Lagos bridge, opened in 1990 and about 11.8 km long, was for years the longest in Africa?
technology.fact: It crosses the Lagos Lagoon to link Lagos Island with the mainland, carrying a huge daily flow of commuters.

technology.q: Which cash crop made Nigeria's Western Region wealthy in the 1950s?
technology.fact: Cocoa revenues helped fund Ibadan's Cocoa House, completed in 1965 and one of the first skyscrapers in tropical Africa.

technology.q: Which mobile operator launched in Nigeria in 2001 and became the country's largest network?
technology.fact: The arrival of GSM networks in 2001 set off a mobile boom that put phones in the hands of well over 100 million Nigerians.

technology.q: Aliko Dangote's industrial group is Africa's largest producer of what?
technology.fact: Dangote Cement runs plants across Africa, with its largest at Obajana in Kogi State.

technology.q: In the 1960s, Kano was famous for towering pyramids of which crop?
technology.fact: Sacks of groundnuts were stacked into pyramids awaiting export, an image that became a symbol of northern farm wealth.

technology.q: Kano's Kofar Mata dye pits, said to date from 1498, colour cloth with which natural dye?
technology.fact: Dyers lower cloth into deep pits of fermented indigo, a craft passed down through families for generations.

technology.q: Nigerian-born Philip Emeagwali won the 1989 Gordon Bell Prize for work in which field?
technology.fact: He used a massively parallel Connection Machine to simulate how oil flows through underground reservoirs.

technology.q: What is Eko Atlantic, being built beside Victoria Island in Lagos?
choices: A new city district on land reclaimed from the sea
technology.fact: It is shielded by a sea wall of huge concrete blocks, nicknamed the 'Great Wall of Lagos'.

technology.q: Ajaokuta in Kogi State is home to a vast plant built to produce what?
technology.fact: Construction began in 1979 with Soviet assistance, but the giant complex has never reached full production.

technology.q: By 1912, a railway linked Lagos with which northern city?
technology.fact: The line helped carry groundnuts and cotton from the north to the coast for export.

technology.q: The Niger Delta's 19th-century 'Oil Rivers' were named after the trade in which product?
technology.fact: Britain proclaimed the Oil Rivers Protectorate in 1884, decades before crude petroleum was found there.

technology.q: In 2014, Dr Stella Ameyo Adadevoh helped stop which disease spreading in Lagos?
technology.fact: By isolating the first Ebola patient to reach Lagos, she helped Nigeria contain the outbreak; she died of the virus herself.

technology.q: Mining on the Jos Plateau historically focused on which metal?
technology.fact: Tin mining took off in the early 1900s, and abandoned mine pits now form lakes across the plateau.

technology.q: In 1959, which city launched Western Nigeria Television, billed as the first TV station in Africa?
technology.fact: WNTV went on air on 31 October 1959 with the proud slogan 'First in Africa'.

technology.q: Which payments company, founded in 2016 by Nigerian entrepreneurs, grew into one of Africa's most valuable tech start-ups?
technology.fact: It helps businesses accept card, bank and mobile-money payments across many African countries.

technology.q: In which year was Nigeria's first satellite, NigeriaSat-1, launched?
technology.fact: Built with Britain's Surrey Satellite Technology, it joined an international constellation that monitors disasters from orbit.

technology.q: Nigeria's first communications satellite, NigComSat-1, launched in 2007, was built by which country?
technology.fact: After the original failed in orbit in 2008, a replacement, NigComSat-1R, was launched in 2011.

technology.q: Nigerian-born car designer Jelani Aliyu led the exterior design of which car?
technology.fact: After years at General Motors, he returned home to lead Nigeria's National Automotive Design and Development Council.

technology.q: Taruga, in central Nigeria, holds some of West Africa's earliest evidence of which technology?
technology.fact: Its ancient furnaces are linked to the Nok culture, which was making iron tools more than 2,000 years ago.

technology.q: Innoson, one of Nigeria's first home-grown carmakers, is based in which south-eastern town?
technology.fact: Nnewi, in Anambra State, is a busy hub for trading and manufacturing vehicle parts.

technology.q: Nigeria's first nuclear research reactor, NIRR-1, commissioned in 2004, is in which university town?
technology.fact: The small reactor at Ahmadu Bello University is used for research and training, and was converted to low-enriched fuel in 2018.

technology.q: Nigeria's first oil refinery opened in 1965 near which city?
technology.fact: The refinery at Alesa-Eleme was built to turn Niger Delta crude into fuel for the domestic market.

art.q: What is the nickname of Nigeria's prolific film industry?
art.fact: By the number of films released, it is often ranked second only to India's film industry.

art.q: Who wrote the 1958 novel 'Things Fall Apart'?
art.fact: Its title comes from W. B. Yeats's poem 'The Second Coming', and it has been translated into more than 50 languages.

art.q: In 1986, which playwright became the first Black African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
art.fact: Soyinka's plays, such as 'Death and the King's Horseman', draw deeply on Yoruba myth and ritual.

art.q: Which musician pioneered Afrobeat in the 1970s?
art.fact: Fela blended highlife, jazz and funk into Afrobeat, with songs that often ran well past ten minutes.

art.q: Which novelist's TED talk 'We Should All Be Feminists' was sampled in a Beyoncé song?
art.fact: Beyoncé quoted the talk on her 2013 track 'Flawless', and Adichie later published it as a short essay.

art.q: Which Nigerian star featured on Drake's 2016 global hit 'One Dance'?
art.fact: 'One Dance' became the first song to pass one billion streams on Spotify.

art.q: What is a gele?
choices: A woman's elaborately tied head wrap
art.fact: Tied from stiff fabric, a gele can rise in dramatic folds and fans at weddings and parties.

art.q: Which hourglass-shaped Yoruba drum can imitate the tones of speech?
art.fact: Squeezing the cords between its two heads tightens the skin, letting a drummer 'speak' the rising and falling tones of Yoruba.

art.q: Which singer of 'Smooth Operator' was born in Ibadan?
art.fact: Born to a Nigerian father and an English mother, Sade moved to England as a child and found fame in the 1980s.

art.q: Despite their name, the Benin Bronzes are mostly made of which alloy?
art.fact: Members of the royal casters' guild, Igun Eronmwon, still work on Igun Street in Benin City.

art.q: Which Nigerian modernist painted 'Tutu' (1974), a portrait of an Ife princess?
art.fact: Long missing, the painting resurfaced in a London flat and sold at auction for £1.2 million in 2018.

art.q: Ben Okri won the 1991 Booker Prize for which novel?
art.fact: At 32, he was then the youngest writer ever to win the Booker.

art.q: Which author wrote 'The Palm-Wine Drinkard' (1952), a fantastical tale drawn from Yoruba folklore?
art.fact: Published in London by Faber and Faber, it was praised by the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas.

art.q: King Sunny Adé is a star of which guitar-driven Yoruba music genre?
art.fact: He added pedal steel guitar and synthesisers to jùjú, and his 1982 album 'Juju Music' won him fans worldwide.

art.q: Lagos's National Theatre, whose shape recalls a military cap, was built for which 1977 festival?
art.fact: FESTAC '77 drew thousands of artists from across Africa and the African diaspora to Lagos.

art.q: Atilogwu, a dazzling acrobatic dance, belongs to which people?
art.fact: Young dancers flip and leap to fast drums and the clang of the ogene metal gong.

art.q: Which 1992 video film is widely credited with launching Nollywood?
art.fact: Shot quickly and sold on VHS tapes, its success inspired a flood of films made straight for the home-video market.

art.q: Adire, made especially in Abeokuta, is what kind of textile?
art.fact: Patterns are created by tying, stitching or painting starch onto cloth before it is dipped in indigo.

art.q: Twins Seven-Seven was a leading artist of which 1960s art movement?
art.fact: Workshops run by Ulli and Georgina Beier helped launch artists who painted vivid scenes from Yoruba myth.

art.q: Uli, flowing line drawings traditionally painted on skin and walls, is an art form of which people?
art.fact: Artists of the Nsukka School, led by Uche Okeke, adapted uli motifs into modern painting.

art.q: Whose 1966 novel 'Efuru' made her one of the first African women novelists published in English internationally?
art.fact: She later founded Tana Press, one of the first publishing houses in Africa run by a woman.

art.q: Which Yoruba music genre was popularised by Sikiru Ayinde Barrister?
art.fact: Barrister said he named the style after Japan's Mount Fuji, which he had seen on a poster.

art.q: Mamman Shata was a celebrated singer and poet in which language?
art.fact: Backed by kalangu talking drums, he built a vast catalogue of songs praising, teasing and chronicling northern life.

art.q: A famous 16th-century ivory pendant mask from Benin depicts which queen mother?
art.fact: Idia, mother of Oba Esigie, was the first Iyoba (queen mother); a copy of the mask became the emblem of FESTAC '77.

art.q: Kwagh-hir, a theatre of puppets and masquerades, comes from which Middle Belt people?
art.fact: Performers use carved puppets, music and dance to act out folk tales, proverbs and satire.

politics.q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
politics.fact: Abuja lies within the Federal Capital Territory, which belongs to none of Nigeria's states.

politics.q: How many states does Nigeria have?
politics.fact: The largest state by area is Niger State, while Lagos State is the smallest.

politics.q: What system of government does Nigeria have?
politics.fact: Power is shared between the federal government and the states, and the president is both head of state and head of government.

politics.q: Who became Nigeria's first President when the country became a republic in 1963?
politics.fact: Known as 'Zik', he had founded the influential West African Pilot newspaper in 1937.

politics.q: Who was Nigeria's first Prime Minister at independence in 1960?
politics.fact: A former teacher from Bauchi, he was admired for his oratory and nicknamed the 'Golden Voice of Africa'.

politics.q: What colours make up Nigeria's national flag?
politics.fact: Student Taiwo Akinkunmi designed it in 1958; the green stands for the land's natural wealth and the white for peace.

politics.q: What is the name of Nigeria's federal legislature?
politics.fact: Its two chambers, the Senate and the House of Representatives, meet in Abuja's Three Arms Zone.

politics.q: Who became president in May 1999, when Nigeria returned to civilian rule?
politics.fact: His inauguration on 29 May 1999 began the period known as the Fourth Republic, and he went on to serve two terms.

politics.q: How long is a Nigerian presidential term?
politics.fact: A president may serve at most two terms, and new terms traditionally begin on 29 May.

politics.q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was founded by a 1975 treaty signed in which city?
politics.fact: ECOWAS now has its headquarters in Abuja.

politics.q: How many seats are there in Nigeria's Senate?
politics.fact: Each of the 36 states elects three senators, and the Federal Capital Territory elects one.

politics.q: On Nigeria's coat of arms, what does the white Y-shaped band represent?
choices: The Niger and Benue rivers meeting
politics.fact: The black shield stands for the country's fertile soil, and the two white horses that support it represent dignity.

politics.q: Nigeria's national motto is 'Unity and Faith, Peace and ...' what?
politics.fact: The motto appears on a ribbon at the base of the national coat of arms.

politics.q: Which Premier of the Western Region introduced free universal primary education there in 1955?
politics.fact: Awolowo's portrait appears on the ₦100 note.

politics.q: Who was the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of the Northern Region?
politics.fact: Ahmadu Bello University in Zaria, founded in 1962, is named after him.

politics.q: The presidential villa in Abuja is popularly named after which nearby granite outcrop?
politics.fact: The 400 m monolith rises behind Abuja's Three Arms Zone, home to the presidency, the National Assembly and the Supreme Court.

politics.q: Which body organises national elections in Nigeria?
politics.fact: The Independent National Electoral Commission was set up in 1998, ahead of the return to civilian rule.

politics.q: In 2017, Nigeria's Amina J. Mohammed became deputy head of which organisation?
politics.fact: Before becoming UN Deputy Secretary-General, she served as Nigeria's environment minister.

politics.q: Which region was carved out of the Western Region in 1963, becoming Nigeria's fourth region?
politics.fact: Created after a referendum, it had its capital at Benin City.

politics.q: Nigeria's 1979 constitution replaced the Westminster-style parliamentary system with what?
politics.fact: Shehu Shagari became the first executive president under the new system in October 1979.

politics.q: How many members sit in Nigeria's House of Representatives?
politics.fact: Members are elected from single-member constituencies for four-year terms.

politics.q: Who became the first woman Speaker of Nigeria's House of Representatives, in 2007?
politics.fact: She represented a constituency in Osun State.

politics.q: Which Nigerian diplomat served as Commonwealth Secretary-General from 1990 to 2000?
politics.fact: He was the first African to hold the post.

politics.q: In 2015, former agriculture minister Akinwumi Adesina was elected president of which institution?
politics.fact: He was re-elected in 2020, and in 2017 he won the World Food Prize.

politics.q: Into how many geopolitical zones is Nigeria commonly grouped?
politics.fact: They are North Central, North East, North West, South East, South South and South West.

current-affairs.q: Who won Nigeria's February 2023 presidential election?
current-affairs.fact: A former governor of Lagos State, he was sworn in on 29 May 2023.

current-affairs.q: Which singer won the Grammy for Best Global Music Album in March 2021 with 'Twice as Tall'?
current-affairs.fact: The Port Harcourt-born star calls himself the 'African Giant', the title of the album before it.

current-affairs.q: In March 2021, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first woman and first African to lead which organisation?
current-affairs.fact: A former Nigerian finance minister, she was reappointed in 2024 for a second term as Director-General.

current-affairs.q: In July 2022, Tobi Amusan set a world record in which athletics event?
current-affairs.fact: She ran 12.12 seconds in the semi-final at the World Championships in Eugene, then won the final to take gold.

current-affairs.q: Victor Osimhen was Serie A's top scorer as which club won the 2022-23 Italian title?
current-affairs.fact: It was Napoli's first league title since 1990, and Osimhen was named 2023 African Footballer of the Year.

current-affairs.q: The giant Dangote Refinery, which began production in 2024, is in which Nigerian state?
current-affairs.fact: Designed to process 650,000 barrels of crude a day, it is billed as the world's largest single-train refinery.

current-affairs.q: In 2023, Lagos chef Hilda Baci set a Guinness World Record for what?
choices: Longest cooking marathon by an individual
Most dishes tasted in an hour
current-affairs.fact: She cooked for about 100 hours non-stop, and Guinness ratified 93 hours and 11 minutes.

current-affairs.q: Which Nigerian singer's 'Calm Down', remixed with Selena Gomez in 2022, became a global hit?
current-affairs.fact: The remix climbed to number three on the US Billboard Hot 100.

current-affairs.q: Nigeria's Super Falcons won the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in July 2025 by beating which host nation 3-2 in the final?
current-affairs.fact: Coming back from 2-0 down, the Falcons claimed a record-extending tenth continental title.

current-affairs.q: Tems earned an Oscar nomination in 2023 as a co-writer of which song from 'Black Panther: Wakanda Forever'?
current-affairs.fact: Sung by Rihanna, the ballad was written as a tribute to the late actor Chadwick Boseman.

current-affairs.q: Ademola Lookman scored a hat-trick in the May 2024 Europa League final for which club?
current-affairs.fact: His three goals ended Leverkusen's 51-match unbeaten run, and he was later named 2024 African Footballer of the Year.

current-affairs.q: In May 2021, Asisat Oshoala became the first African woman to win the UEFA Women's Champions League, with which club?
current-affairs.fact: Barcelona beat Chelsea 4-0 in the final in Gothenburg.

current-affairs.q: In June 2021, a new standard-gauge railway was commissioned linking Lagos with which city?
current-affairs.fact: The line, about 157 km long, is planned as the first stage of a network running north to Kano.

current-affairs.q: The Second Niger Bridge, commissioned in May 2023, connects Asaba with which city?
current-affairs.fact: About 1.6 km long, it eases traffic on the original Niger Bridge, opened in 1965.

current-affairs.q: In May 2024, Nigeria brought back which national anthem, first sung at independence?
current-affairs.fact: It replaced 'Arise, O Compatriots', which had been the anthem since 1978.

current-affairs.q: Who won Nigeria's February 2019 presidential election?
current-affairs.fact: It was Buhari's second victory, following his first presidential win in 2015.

current-affairs.q: In April 2024, Nigerian chess champion Tunde Onakoya set a world record for the longest chess marathon in which city?
current-affairs.fact: Playing for about 58 hours in Times Square, he raised funds for children's education through his Chess in Slums Africa initiative.

current-affairs.q: Nigeria reached the final of the Africa Cup of Nations held in early 2024. Which team beat them 2-1?
current-affairs.fact: The hosts came from behind in Abidjan to win their third continental title.

current-affairs.q: In September 2023, which Lagos rail line began carrying passengers as the city's first electric light-rail service?
current-affairs.fact: Its first phase runs from Marina on Lagos Island to Mile 2 on the mainland.

current-affairs.q: Which US payments company bought the Lagos start-up Paystack in 2020?
current-affairs.fact: The deal, reported at over $200 million, was then one of the largest acquisitions of a Nigerian start-up.

current-affairs.q: In April 2019, which Lagos-founded online retailer became the first African tech start-up listed on the New York Stock Exchange?
current-affairs.fact: Jumia launched in Lagos in 2012 and expanded its online marketplace to many African countries.

current-affairs.q: Nigeria's first deep-sea port, commissioned in January 2023, is at which location?
current-affairs.fact: Built in the Lekki Free Zone east of Lagos, its deep berths can take far larger container ships than the older city ports.

current-affairs.q: In January 2025, Nigeria became a partner country of which group?
current-affairs.fact: Brazil, which chaired the bloc that year, announced Nigeria as its newest partner country.

current-affairs.q: Which actor-director's 'A Tribe Called Judah' (2023) became the first Nollywood film to earn over ₦1 billion in cinemas?
current-affairs.fact: Akindele, also known for her 'Jenifa' comedy franchise, co-directed and starred in the film.

current-affairs.q: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's first novel in over a decade, published in March 2025, is titled what?
current-affairs.fact: The novel follows four women whose lives and friendships stretch between Africa and America.

general.q: Nigeria is the most populous country on which continent?
general.fact: With well over 200 million people, it ranks among the ten most populous countries in the world.

general.q: What is Nigeria's largest city?
general.fact: Its name is Portuguese for 'lakes', and locals also know the city as Eko.

general.q: What is Nigeria's currency?
general.fact: Introduced in 1973 to replace the Nigerian pound, the naira is divided into 100 kobo.

general.q: Which tomato-rich rice dish sparks a friendly rivalry between Nigeria and Ghana?
general.fact: Its name comes from the Wolof (Jolof) people of Senegambia, where the dish is thought to have originated.

general.q: What is Nigeria's official language?
general.fact: Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo are each spoken by tens of millions, and Nigerian Pidgin is a popular common tongue.

general.q: What is the nickname of Nigeria's men's national football team?
general.fact: Known as the Green Eagles until the late 1980s, the team has won the Africa Cup of Nations three times.

general.q: Which lake does Nigeria share with Chad, Niger and Cameroon?
general.fact: The shallow lake has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s, by as much as 90% by some estimates.

general.q: What is suya, a favourite Nigerian street food?
general.fact: Of Hausa origin, it is coated in yaji, a spice mix made with ground peanuts and chilli.

general.q: Which NBA Hall of Famer, nicknamed 'The Dream', was born in Lagos?
general.fact: He led the Houston Rockets to back-to-back NBA titles in 1994 and 1995.

general.q: Which river joins the Niger at Lokoja?
general.fact: Lokoja, overlooking the confluence, was an early base of British administration in the north around 1900.

general.q: Which huge granite monolith near Abuja appears on the ₦100 note?
general.fact: Rising about 300 m above the surrounding plain, it is nicknamed the 'Gateway to Abuja'.

general.q: At which Olympic Games did Nigeria win gold in men's football?
general.fact: The 'Dream Team' beat Brazil in the semi-final and Argentina 3-2 in the final, the first Olympic football gold for an African nation.

general.q: Yankari, famous for its elephants and Wikki Warm Springs, is in which state?
general.fact: The crystal-clear spring stays at around 31 °C all year, making a swim a highlight of any safari there.

general.q: The Iri Ji festival of the Igbo celebrates the harvest of which crop?
general.fact: The first new yams are traditionally blessed and eaten by elders or a ruler before anyone else may enjoy them.

general.q: Which city hosts a December carnival billed as 'Africa's biggest street party'?
general.fact: Cross River State's capital stages parades of rival costumed bands, drawing visitors from across the world.

general.q: Which Middle Belt city, on a high plateau, is known for its cool climate?
general.fact: At around 1,200 m above sea level, it is one of Nigeria's coolest cities and a centre for growing potatoes.

general.q: Roughly how many languages are spoken in Nigeria?
general.fact: That makes Nigeria one of the most linguistically diverse countries on Earth.

general.q: What is the central spectacle of a northern Nigerian Durbar festival?
choices: A parade of richly dressed horsemen
general.fact: Held in cities such as Kano, Katsina and Zaria during Sallah celebrations, it sees cavalry charge up to salute the emir.

general.q: Which hilltop landscape in Adamawa State was the first African cultural landscape on the World Heritage List?
general.fact: Terraced fields, stone paths and the chief's palace crown the hill in the Mandara Mountains.

general.q: The Argungu Festival in Kebbi State centres on what kind of competition?
general.fact: Thousands of fishermen leap into the river with nets and gourds, competing to land the biggest fish.

general.q: The Eyo festival, with its white-robed masquerades, is held in which city?
general.fact: The masqueraders wear flowing white robes and wide-brimmed hats and are also known as 'Adamu Orisha'.

general.q: What is the highest peak in Nigeria?
general.fact: At about 2,419 m, it rises in the Gotel Mountains of Taraba State, on the border with Cameroon.

general.q: The Lekki Conservation Centre in Lagos is known for Africa's longest what?
general.fact: The swaying walkway, about 400 m long, lets visitors stroll above mangrove and swamp forest.

general.q: Which rock in Abeokuta once sheltered the Egba people and gave the city its name?
general.fact: Abeokuta means 'under the rock' in Yoruba.

general.q: In 1996, who became the first Nigerian to win an Olympic gold medal?
general.fact: She won the long jump in Atlanta, two days before the men's football team also struck gold.
